LTOS> TYPE README.TXT
LTOS 0.5 - LiteOS for the Elf2K, running in your browser.

The real kernel, shell and programs, on an emulated RCA 1802 with a CF card.
Some things to try:

  HELP              every command          HELP SCRIPTS   what a script can do
  DIR /BIN          the programs           TYPE DEMO.SH   a shell script
  DEMO you          run DEMO.SH            SH -x TEST     each line shown as it runs
  LW2 DOCS/LETTER.TXT                      the Lite-Writer 2 editor (^X: menu)
  GALAXIA           a game (arrows, SPACE; Esc quits back to LTOS)
  ORBIT             STELLAR ORBIT: fly Apollo 7 on three VMs (SPACE starts the count)
  EROFF EROFF.RF    a small nroff: plain text made into pages (> EROFF.TXT keeps it)
  SORT -n -r DOCS/SALES.TXT    SORT, UNIQ, PWD, WC, GREP ... - HELP has them all
  RAWK '{ s += $2 } END { print s }' DOCS/SALES.TXT
  ECHO hello > HI.TXT ; TYPE HI.TXT ; FSCK

Changes you make stay in this browser. "Restore the card" puts every file back.
LTOS> TEST
Testing the batch feature
1
2
3
LTOS> SH -x TEST
+ echo "Testing the batch feature"
Testing the batch feature
+ echo "1"
1
+ echo "2"
2
+ echo "3"
3
+ exit

LTOS> HELP SCRIPTS
SCRIPTS - What a .SH script can hold

  # a comment               cmd1; cmd2         two commands on one line
  NAME=value  (no spaces)   $NAME ${NAME}      a variable (names exact)
  $0 the script  $1-$9 its words  $# how many  $? the last status (0 = ok)
  'single quotes': nothing changes inside;  "double": $NAME is replaced
  echo [-n] words           read [-p "prompt "] NAME    (a line typed)
  if [ "$1" = DOCS ]; then ... elif ...; then ... else ... fi
  test / [ ]:  -z -n text   a = b  a != b   -eq -ne -lt -le -gt -ge
               -e -f -d -s name (there, a file, a folder, not empty)  !
  true  false  exit [n]  set (the variables; -x, +x)  unset NAME
Any other line is a command, as typed at the prompt (> files too).
HELP LOOPS: while, for, arithmetic and the rest.

  read -p "Folder? " F
  if [ -d "$F" ]; then DIR $F > LIST.TXT; else echo no $F; fi
